sar.narrative: This suspicious activity report documents confirmed card-not-present fraud identified on card C08318-K1 under customer C08318. On 2016-12-14 at 13:41:14 UTC, unauthorized online transaction 3541817 in the amount of $450.09 for product R was executed in billing region 126. The transaction was initiated using device D007135, profiled as a Windows 10 system running Edge 16.0 (resolution 1365x768), which was recorded as new to the account. Internal model monitoring flagged the transaction with a model score of 0.993, representing a 92.1 percent historical fraud rate. Knowledge graph analysis identified that device D007135 was concurrently used on 2016-12-12 on card C07196-K2 to conduct matching transaction 3536052 for $450.06 for product R. In addition, device D007135 is linked to three prior closed confirmed fraud cases, CC-5329, CC-5557, and CC-5430, involving card C06224-K2. Cardholder C08318 had no prior established transaction history or baseline with device D007135. The execution of near-identical transactions across multiple unrelated cards from the same device demonstrates deliberate and unauthorized card-not-present activity. Total fraudulent exposure resulting from this transaction is $450.09. The bank has blocked card C08318-K1 to prevent further losses, placed connected card C07196-K2 on heightened monitoring, and filed this report.

Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

Known pattern 2: Card-not-present fraud. The number is used online without the card. Amounts and products that don't fit the cardholder's history, often in a burst of two to four within 48 hours. On its own, one unusual online purchase is ambiguous: verify. Policy R1 to R4.

passages.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
passages.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

Investigation into device D007135 reveals a clear shared origin (lift 36.33 vs all transactions) with card C07196-K2, which conducted transactions of nearly identical amounts and product type ($450.06 on transaction 3536052, scoring 0.997) two days prior on 2016-12-12. Furthermore, device D007135 is linked to three prior closed confirmed fraud cases (CC-5329, CC-5557, CC-5430). While the cardholder has no prior transaction history and community lift is 0.0, the tight cross-card link, shared device origin, matching transaction pattern, and high calibrated model score confirm card-not-present fraud from a new device.
